$comment: Network policy for the AWS MCP proxy container, enforced by ToolHive's
egress proxy rather than by trusting the process to behave.
This container is the only component holding AWS credentials, which makes
its egress worth constraining: if it can only reach the AWS MCP endpoint
and STS, then a compromised or misbehaving proxy has nowhere to send them.
Cursor never receives these credentials at all, so this is defence for the
Not the authorization boundary. What the agent may DO in AWS is decided by
the IAM policy on nkb-agent-readonly-alpha, and the baseline proved that
holds independently: a policy simulation returned explicitDeny for
sqs:DeleteQueue. This file only limits where packets may go.
